Subject: AtlasBank: high-level question on cache locality for private deployment

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. One quick follow-up from our infra team: for our EU customers we need strong guarantees that inference cache segments (prefix cache and KV layers) never egress to APAC regions unless explicitly authorized. From the demo it looked like there are optimizations that allow cross-region cache fills — can you confirm whether we can disable cross-region cache-population while still keeping warm caches locally?

Also attaching a rough diagram of our expected traffic flows (attachment: atlas_regional_cache_map.pdf). Can we get a short note describing how Redwood handles:
- cache population across warm standby pools
- forced locality for KV caches
- cache invalidation/TTL propagation across regions

Would appreciate a reply by early next week so we can add to our compliance intake.

Best,
Jorge
VP, Cloud Engineering
AtlasBank
From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Jorge Sosa <jorge.sosa@atlasbank.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AtlasBank: high-level question on cache locality for private deployment

Jorge — thanks for the diagram, very helpful. Short answers up front, full notes below.

- Yes, we can configure strict cache-locality so that no cache population crosses region boundaries. That is a deployment-time policy on Redwood Private routing + runtime.
- Warm caches are still supported locally; we ship per-region cache warmers and optional cross-region pre-warming (disabled in your case).
- TTLs and invalidation are configurable: you can choose local-only invalidation or a brokered control plane that propagates invalidation events (we recommend local-only for strongest residency guarantees).

Detailed notes (internal/tech):
1) Runtime topology controls
   - Each Private deployment defines region-scoped cache domains. The runtime exposes a policy flag cache.domain.scope = {local, global} at deploy-time. For AtlasBank we would set this to local.
   - Local mode: all KV writes and prefix cache fills are pinned to regional storage/redis instances; replication is disabled.

2) Routing / Smart routing implications
   - Smart routing still operates for model selection and fallbacks but will respect cache.domain.scope. If a region is out of capacity, requests can failover to an APAC model variant, but cached state remains local and is not pulled across.

3) Warm standby & priming
   - We run per-region cache priming jobs (k8s CronJobs in the customer's VPC) that populate local caches from a snapshot export. Cross-region snapshot fetch is optional and can be blocked via network ACLs.

4) Audit/evidence
   - We can produce a deployment verification report showing cache.domain.scope settings, control-plane logs of cache-related RPCs, and network flow logs demonstrating zero cross-region cache traffic for a 48h window.

Attachments: atlas_regional_cache_map.pdf (from you), plus a short risk matrix I prepared: localization-risk-matrix.xlsx

Let me know if you want a quick call this week to review the verification artifacts.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
